facts.quote: On April 19, 2024, AT&T Inc. (“AT&T”) learned that a threat actor claimed to have unlawfully accessed and copied AT&T call logs.

Based on its investigation, AT&T believes that threat actors unlawfully accessed an AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform and, between April 14 and April 25, 2024, exfiltrated files containing AT&T records of customer call and text interactions that occurred between approximately May 1 and October 31, 2022, as well as on January 2, 2023, as described below.
facts.note: Stated as the start of the exfiltration window (April 14 to April 25, 2024), not explicitly the start of the intrusion.

facts.quote: Based on its investigation, AT&T believes that threat actors unlawfully accessed an AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform and, between April 14 and April 25, 2024, exfiltrated files containing AT&T records of customer call and text interactions that occurred between approximately May 1 and October 31, 2022, as well as on January 2, 2023, as described below.

facts.value: customer call and text interaction records (metadata, no content, no SSNs or PII)
facts.quote: Current analysis indicates that the data includes, for these periods of time, records of calls and texts of nearly all of AT&T’s wireless customers and customers of mobile virtual network operators (“MVNO”) using AT&T’s wireless network.
facts.note: Filing says data does not contain call/text content, Social Security numbers, dates of birth or other PII; includes phone numbers interacted with, counts, aggregate duration, and for a subset cell site IDs.

facts.value: AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform
facts.quote: Based on its investigation, AT&T believes that threat actors unlawfully accessed an AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform and, between April 14 and April 25, 2024, exfiltrated files containing AT&T records of customer call and text interactions that occurred between approximately May 1 and October 31, 2022, as well as on January 2, 2023, as described below.
facts.note: The filing names where access occurred (a third-party cloud workspace), not how the threat actor got in; no credential, vulnerability or vendor-compromise mechanism is stated.

facts.note: This is the system that was compromised. The affected data population is nearly all AT&T wireless customers and MVNO customers on AT&T's wireless network (see DATA_TYPE_AFFECTED and CUSTOMER_OR_THIRD_PARTY_IMPACT).

facts.value: nearly all wireless and MVNO customers' call/text records taken; AT&T will notify impacted customers
facts.quote: AT&T will provide notice to its current and former impacted customers.
facts.note: Also notes that although names are not included, publicly available tools can often link a number to a name.

facts.quote: As of the date of this filing, this incident has not had a material impact on AT&T’s operations, and AT&T does not believe that this incident is reasonably likely to materially impact AT&T’s financial condition or results of operations.
facts.note: Filing says no material impact on operations; no disruption is described.

facts.quote: As of the date of this filing, this incident has not had a material impact on AT&T’s operations, and AT&T does not believe that this incident is reasonably likely to materially impact AT&T’s financial condition or results of operations.
AT&T has taken additional cybersecurity measures in response to this incident including closing off the point of unlawful access.
facts.note: Point of access closed; the word 'contained' is not used.

facts.quote: AT&T immediately activated its incident response process to investigate and retained external cybersecurity experts to assist.
AT&T is working with law enforcement in its efforts to arrest those involved in the incident.
On May 9, 2024, and again on June 5, 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice determined that, under Item 1.05(c) of Form 8-K, a delay in providing public disclosure was warranted.
facts.note: The U.S. Department of Justice was engaged twice to make the Item 1.05(c) delay determination, which requires the company to have brought the incident to the government; DOJ is also a law enforcement body. The filing does not use the word 'notified'.

facts.value: DOJ-authorized disclosure delay ended; filing now timely

summary: AT&T discloses that threat actors accessed an AT&T workspace on a third-party cloud platform and, between April 14 and 25, 2024, exfiltrated call and text metadata records for nearly all wireless and MVNO customers covering mid-2022 and January 2, 2023; disclosure was delayed twice at DOJ request, at least one person has been apprehended, and AT&T says the incident is not material to its operations, financial condition or results.
